text: Yes, the 2021 tree-cover loss was caused by timber harvest of the pine plantation. The affected area (81.3 ha) was nearly all (98%) mapped as forest in 2020 by the JRC, and the Uruguayan MGAP forest map confirms it was entirely planted pine (68.1 ha of *Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*), with no native forest involved. The loss was observed in a single year (2021) and met the 0.5-ha minimum event size, ruling out small-scale or scattered disturbances. While 37.3 ha of smaller patches were flagged as non-events, the remaining 44 ha clearly aligns with industrial harvest patterns in plantations.
